instruction: Switch to the Amazon homepage tab and make it the active tab in Chrome.

metadata.explanation: Task requires switching to the Amazon homepage tab to make it active. Uses existing is_expected_active_tab metric to verify amazon.com homepage is the active tab.
metadata.verification: The is_expected_active_tab function checks if the active tab URL matches the expected URL. Returns 1.0 if amazon.com homepage is active, 0.0 otherwise.

llm_judge_reasons: The getter 'active_tab_info' has a semantic flaw: it reloads the active tab URL instead of just reading the current tab state
The getter uses get_active_url_from_accessTree to find the active URL, then navigates to it using Playwright, which triggers a page reload
The code explicitly warns (chrome.py:806-809): 'This function will reload the target-url page. If the target url has cache or cookie, this function may reload to another page.'
For URL verification tasks, reloading the page is unnecessary and introduces risk of navigation side effects
The metric logic itself (is_expected_active_tab) is correct for URL comparison
Expected value 'https://www.amazon.com/' is semantically correct for the Amazon homepage
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change the result getter from 'active_tab_info' to 'active_url_from_accessTree' which only reads the URL from accessibility tree without navigation
Update the evaluator to use type: 'active_url' instead of 'active_tab_info', or create a new getter that extracts active tab URL without reloading
Alternatively, use the metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' which can work with just a URL string from get_active_url_from_accessTree
The current setup may still work if Amazon.com doesn't redirect on reload, but it's fragile and semantically incorrect for a 'check active tab' task
